newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait's KOTC to order three tankers.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait's KOTC to order three tankers.

text.p: State-owned Kuwait Oil Tanker Co (KOTC) said on Wednesday it was close to awarding a contract to build three 290,000-tonne tankers.
Sheikh Salman al-Sabah, a deputy chairman at KOTC, also told a news conference the company had received 15 offers by major shipbuilders but did not give the projected value for the deal.
He said the deal would be awarded soon.
KOTC "wants to make a comprehensive study...to decide how many tankers we need and what are the tankers that we can dispose of," he said.
KOTC has a 33-strong fleet which includes 22 oil product tankers with a total capacity of 1.6 million tonnes and five crude tankers with a combined capacity of 1.4 million tonnes.

The supertanker Bridgeton was sold last week for $11.3 million, while the company plans to sell as scrap in a few months the 19-year-old, 268,000-tonne Tonbridge crude tanker and the 23-year-old al-Wataniah products tanker, Sheikh Salman said.
KOTC's net profit fell 0.8 percent to 8.5 million dinars ($28.4 million) in fiscal 1995/96 (July-June), according to official figures released at the news conference.
KOTC carries about 20 percent of Kuwait's oil exports. Kuwait has an OPEC production quota of two million barrels per day.
KOTC is the shipping arm of the state Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC) which oversees the entire oil sector.
